title: Comparing named vendors for an email-delivery provider decision
notes: Session mentioning many named products, vendors, and people while evaluating an email-delivery provider. Mirrors fx13's entity-rich structure; tests whether atom text stays faithful and specific with many named entities in play.

turns.text: We need to pick a transactional email provider. I know Priya already looked at SendGrid and Postmark — what's the state of that comparison?

Per Priya's notes: SendGrid offers the broadest feature set (marketing + transactional in one platform) but has a worse reputation for deliverability lately due to shared IP pool issues reported by several users on their status page. Postmark is transactional-only, deliverability-focused, and Priya's test sends landed in inbox 98% of the time versus SendGrid's 91% in the same test.
What about Amazon SES? We're already on AWS for everything else.

SES is the cheapest by far and integrates natively with our existing AWS infrastructure (same IAM roles, CloudWatch metrics), but it requires more manual setup for things like bounce/complaint handling and templating that Postmark and SendGrid provide out of the box.
Did we ever loop in security about any of these regarding data residency?

Yes — Marcus from security confirmed Postmark and SES both support EU data residency (Postmark via their EU region, SES via eu-west-1), which matters for the GDPR-covered customers we onboarded last quarter. SendGrid's EU offering was less clear and Marcus flagged it as needing more diligence before we could greenlight it for those customers.
Given all that, let's go with Postmark.

Going with Postmark — best deliverability in Priya's test (98% inbox rate), confirmed EU data residency per Marcus, and transactional-focused feature set that matches our actual need better than SendGrid's broader marketing-oriented platform.
